'''Tasha Rose Inniss''' is an American [[mathematician]] and the vice [[provost (education)|provost]] for research at [[Spelman College]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Tasha Inniss, Ph.D. Biography |journal=Spelman College |url=https://www.spelman.edu/staff/profiles/tasha-inniss.html |access-date=17 August 2025}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Inniss was born in [[New Orleans]] and grew up without a father.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/underrepresented-minorities-science-statistical-anomaly-story-african-american-woman|title=Underrepresented Minorities in Science: A Statistical Anomaly: The Story of an African-American Woman Battling the Odds to Become a Mathematician|date=2001-03-02|work=Science {{!}} AAAS|access-date=2018-05-05|language=en}}</ref> She became interested in mathematics in fourth grade, and decided she would study it as a freshman in high school.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Complexities : women in mathematics|title-link= Complexities: Women in Mathematics |date=2005|publisher=Princeton University Press|editor1=Case, Bettye Anne |editor2=[[Anne M. Leggett|Leggett, Anne M.]]|isbn=978-1400880164|location=Princeton, N.J.|oclc=949753960}}</ref> She studied mathematics at [[Xavier University of Louisiana]], graduating [[summa cum laude]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/student-essay-contest/2001-student-essay-contest-results/|title=Student Essay Contest: 2001 Results|website=awm-math.org|access-date=2019-02-24}}</ref> In 1992 she was listed in the ''Who's Who Among Colleges and Universities'' for her academic achievements.<ref name=":0" /> She earned a master's degree in applied mathematics from Georgia Institute of Technology.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.informs.org/About-INFORMS/News-Room/Press-Releases/INFORMS-adds-new-Director-of-Education-and-Industry-Outreach-to-Leadership-Team|title=INFORMS adds new Director of Education and Industry Outreach to Leadership Team|last=INFORMS|website=INFORMS|language=en-US|access-date=2018-05-05|archive-date=2022-06-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220627151600/https://www.informs.org/About-INFORMS/News-Room/Press-Releases/INFORMS-adds-new-Director-of-Education-and-Industry-Outreach-to-Leadership-Team|url-status=dead}}</ref>

She moved to the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]] for her PhD, funded by the [[David and Lucile Packard Foundation]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.deltasee.org/radio/radio_bio101-105.htm|title=Delta SEE: About Us|website=www.deltasee.org|access-date=2018-05-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ehrweb.aaas.org/packard/site/schools/details.php?sid=58|title=Packard Foundation Graduate Scholars Program: HBCU Directory|website=ehrweb.aaas.org|access-date=2018-05-05}}</ref> In 2000, Inniss became the first African American woman to obtain a Ph.D. in mathematics from the University of Maryland, together with Sherry Scott and [[Kimberly Weems]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.umd.edu/~rlj/tks.html|title=The First Three African American Women to Receive Doctorates in the Mathematics Department|website=www.math.umd.edu|access-date=2018-05-05}}</ref> Her dissertation was ''Stochastic Models for the Estimation of Airport Arrival Capacity Distributions''. She was part of the [[National Center of Excellence for Aviation Operators]] and advised by Michael Owen Ball.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=66671}}</ref> Her brother, Enos Inniss, also completed his PhD in 2000.<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career ==
In 2001 she was appointed the [[Clare Boothe Luce]] Professor of Mathematics at [[Trinity Washington University]].<ref name=":0" /> Her doctoral thesis described programming methods to calibrate models to estimate airport capacity.<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Tasha|first=Inniss|date=2001|publisher=University of Maryland|title=Stochastic Models for the Estimation of Airport Arrival Capacity Distributions|hdl=1903/6256|type=PhD thesis}}</ref> She remains a consultant for the [[Federal Aviation Administration]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.duchessinternationalmagazine.com/profile/tasha-r-inniss/|title=Tasha R. Inniss|website=Duchess International Magazine|access-date=2018-05-05}}</ref>

She joined the department of mathematics at [[Spelman College]] in 2005 as an assistant professor.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Inniss|first1=Tasha R.|last2=Lee|first2=John R.|last3=Light|first3=Marc|last4=Grassi|first4=Michael A.|last5=Thomas|first5=George|last6=Williams|first6=Andrew B.|title=Proceedings of the 1st international workshop on Text mining in bioinformatics |chapter=Towards applying text mining and natural language processing for biomedical ontology acquisition |date=2006-11-10|url=http://dl.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=1183535.1183539|publisher=ACM|pages=7–14|doi=10.1145/1183535.1183539|isbn=978-1595935267|s2cid=2365000}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://livingthinkers.com/Interviewees.html|title=Interviewees|work=livingthinkers|access-date=2018-05-05|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Muicahy|first=Colm|title=A Century of Mathematical Excellence at Spelman College|date=2017|url=http://digitalcommons.auctr.edu/scpubs/13/|journal=A Century of Mathematical Excellence at Spelman College|language=en|publisher=Atlanta University Center, Robert W. Woodruff Library|doi=10.22595/scpubs.00013|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Throughout her career she has worked to recruit, support and mentor underrepresented minority students.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=L.|first=Joiner, Lottie|date=2003-01-05|title=Success to the Third Degree.|url=https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ631197|journal=Black Issues in Higher Education|language=en|volume=18|issue=11|issn=0742-0277}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.questia.com/magazine/1P4-2007478324/hbcus-relevance-in-diversifying-the-stem-workforce|title="HBCUs' Relevance in Diversifying the STEM Workforce" by Carter-Johnson, Frances; Inniss, Tasha; Lee, Mark E. - Diverse Issues in Higher Education, Vol. 35, Issue 2, February 22, 2018|website=|language=en|access-date=|archive-date=May 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180506103941/https://www.questia.com/magazine/1P4-2007478324/hbcus-relevance-in-diversifying-the-stem-workforce|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.umass.edu/newsoffice/article/against-odds-three-african-american-women-discuss-road-math-phds|title=Against the Odds: Three African-American Women to Discuss the Road to Math Ph.D.s|work=Office of News & Media Relations {{!}} UMass Amherst|access-date=2018-05-05|language=en|archive-date=2018-12-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181210111207/https://www.umass.edu/newsoffice/article/against-odds-three-african-american-women-discuss-road-math-phds|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.aacu.org/publications-research/periodicals/who-minding-gap|title=Who Is Minding the Gap?|last=Review|first=Peer|date=2014-04-29|work=Association of American Colleges & Universities|access-date=2018-05-05|language=en|archive-date=2018-05-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180506042123/https://www.aacu.org/publications-research/periodicals/who-minding-gap|url-status=dead}}</ref> She led a [[National Science Foundation]] project that looked to ''increase the quality and quantity of underrepresented minorities matriculating and completing doctoral degrees.''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1249262|title=NSF Award Search: Award#1249262 - Bridge to the Doctorate at UMCP, 2012-2014|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2018-05-05}}</ref> She has contributed to the [[EDGE Foundation]] (Enhancing Diversity in Graduate Education) program.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.edgeforwomen.org/edge-2009/|title=EDGE 2009|work=THE EDGE PROGRAM|access-date=2018-05-05|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2017 she joined the [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]] as Director of Education.<ref name=":2" />

Inniss' work earned her recognition by [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] as a Black History Month 2017 Honoree.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tasha Inniss|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/tasha-inniss/|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black}}</ref>

In 2022, Inniss was added to the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS) Committee on Professional Ethics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/profethics-past.html |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>
